 The Invesco QQQ Trust is down about 0.7% overnight at around 640.6, after closing near 645. The daily line chart shows a sharp slide from the high near 760 in late October, with price now roughly 15% below that peak and back at levels last seen in early summer. The drop came in two steps: a fast fall to about 665, a short bounce to 690, and then another leg down that took out the 660 area. What stands out is the volume. The heaviest bars of the past few months are clustered at the end of this decline, which points to real selling rather than a quiet pullback. Tech-heavy indexes like QQQ tend to move harder than the broader market, so a drop of this size says growth stocks are carrying most of the pressure. My plan is to stay patient and not guess the bottom. I'm watching 620 as the next support, where the chart showed a pause earlier this year. A daily close back above 665 would be the first sign that buyers are returning, and 700 would be the level to reclaim before I trust the uptrend again. The market is focused on rate expectations and whether AI and big tech earnings can justify these valuations, and both can swing QQQ quickly in either direction. Do you see this as a normal pullback in a bull market, or the start of a deeper correction in tech? Disclaimer: Community is offered by Moomoo Technologies Inc. and is for educational purposes only.
